summary.headline: Tinna Rubber Q1 FY27 posted record EBITDA above INR50 crores (21%+ margin) and PAT above INR20 crores, with EPR credits adding a one-off monetisation lift.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q1 FY27 profitability, with standalone and consolidated EBITDA margins above 21% and PAT margins above 13%. Standalone revenue rose 18% YoY and consolidated revenue rose 20%, with EBITDA margin up 638 bps standalone and 575 bps consolidated. Management attributed the margin gain mainly to gross margin expansion from cheaper feedstock and a higher mix of value-added products such as MRP and reclaimed rubber. Growth engines (PCMB, TPO/rCB, Oman, South Africa) are still ramping, and management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR670-700 crores and a sustainable 18-20% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 58% YoY; MRP volumes +28% and reclaimed rubber volumes +37% YoY; run-rate cited at INR45-46 crores per quarter. Exports volume +46% YoY.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Revenue +7% YoY; volumes +33% YoY on rubberized bitumen demand amid bitumen shortage. Secured a 15,000 tonne rubberized bitumen processing order for FY27. Bitumen emulsion hit by supply constraints.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Volumes declined (analyst cited ~20%); binder and synthetic grass prices rose up to threefold, delaying turfing projects. Management says consumer is ~8-10% of business.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Revenue steady with marginal volume decline, supported by price corrections. Exclusive India distributorship for Zibo TAA Metal Technology steel abrasives; ~50% volume growth targeted in FY27.

segments.name: Tire recycling (India and Oman)
segments.commentary: India capacity utilisation 88%, volumes +35% YoY but down 10% QoQ on softer consumer demand. Oman utilisation 78%, hit by West Asia conflict.

segments.name: PCMB / PP Buildtech
segments.commentary: PCMB at 82% utilisation of initial 6,000 tpa; total capacity 18,000 tpa after Haryana expansion; targeted ~10% of FY27 revenue. Kolkata plant commissioned Q4 FY26; targeting >30% growth and INR100 crores revenue in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reiterated at INR670-700 crores (INR675-700 crores cited in later reply).
EBITDA margin guidance of 18-20% for FY27, described as sustainable despite Q1 at ~22%; management declined to confirm either 18% or 22%.
Vision 2029: INR1,000 crores revenue by FY29, 25%+ revenue CAGR, 33%+ profitability CAGR, EBITDA margin above 18%, ROCE above 30%, presence in 10 locations.
Capex of ~INR100 crores across FY27-FY28; INR27 crores spent in Q1 FY27; ~INR60 crores to be capitalised in FY27. Capex could rise if demand stays strong.
TPO/rCB (pyrolysis oil and recovered carbon black) contribution of 7-10% of FY27 revenue (~INR50-60 crores). TPO sales from Q2 FY27; rCB production from Q3 FY27.

South Africa breakeven expected Q2 FY27; Phase 2 tyre crumb production expected Q2 or Q3 FY27. Saudi Arabia (24,000 tpa) construction targeted toward end of calendar 2026, subject to Middle East normalisation.
Expansion of India tyre crushing capacity to 235,000 tpa (+27%) by FY27; MRP capacity 3,500 tpa addition by Q3 FY27 to 20,000 tpa total.
capex_capacity: India tyre crushing capacity 185,000 tpa, rising to 235,000 tpa by FY27 (+27%).
MRP capacity: 3,500 tpa expansion commissioning by Q3 FY27, taking total to 20,000 tpa.
TPO plant at Varle: trials began Q1 FY27; commercial sales Q2 FY27; stabilisation by Q3 FY27. rCB production Q3 FY27, commercial sales by Q4 FY27.
Rooftop solar: Gummidipoondi 999 kW (June 2026) and Varle 2,218 kW (July 2026). Renewable capacity raised from 1.23 MW to 4.48 MW; renewables were 51% of power in Q1 FY27.
Management is exploring de-bottlenecking and possibly a greenfield India plant; India utilisation cited at 80-85% by analyst. Blended utilisation target 75-80% by year-end across geographies.
demand_pricing: Industrial demand supported by rising raw material costs and ESG-driven tyre-maker demand; MRP and reclaimed rubber volumes growing fast.
Rubberized bitumen demand rose as bitumen supply tightened and prices rose due to the West Asia conflict; government push to reduce import dependence.
Consumer turfing demand hit by binder and synthetic grass price spikes; management says the market is intact and will recover once prices stabilise.
EPR credits: ~100,000 units monetised in Q1 at a floor price of ~INR2,500 per unit (~INR25 crores cash). Management says EPR contributes ~INR25-30 crores a year at PBT level.
Margin gain attributed to raw material optionality and value-added product mix. Management said inventory gains were very marginal.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin rise is due to inventory gains, and is there margin normalisation ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gains were very marginal. Management said the changes are systemic (raw material optionality, value-added mix), and expects some front-ended costs from new projects, so 18-20% is the sustainable range.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the 400-500 bps margin expansion; material plus inventory cost fell to 46% of sales.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main contribution came at gross margin, from cheaper raw material and higher realisation from value-added products, plus scale efficiencies. Overall EBITDA margin expanded about 4 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: How is EPR monetisation accounted for, and what is its contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said accrued EPR credits from prior years were monetised against unbilled revenue. Q1 P&L impact was already booked in FY26. Annual EPR contribution is about INR25-30 crores at PBT level. Analysts' questions on clean PAT were not fully resolved on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Chile and Saudi Arabia, and will overseas investment scale up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Oman's limited scope and similar operating parameters for Saudi Arabia, and end-of-life tyre sourcing and hedging for South Africa and Chile. India remains the core investment focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for infrastructure given the West Asia situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bitumen shortages hit some projects, but rubberized asphalt demand rose as contractors sought cheaper alternatives. Infrastructure revenue grew 7% in Q1, and Q1 is the peak road-work season.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue guidance of INR670-700 crores was reiterated; margin should sustain at 18-20% even though Q1 was 22%.

risks_watch: Earnings quality: the INR21 crore EPR monetisation and its treatment in the P&L were unclear on the call; analysts could not get a clean recurring PAT.
Other expenses rose ~INR5.4 crores QoQ per analyst; company promised an email clarification.
Geopolitical risk (West Asia conflict) affecting bitumen and binder supply, Oman utilisation (78%), and the Saudi project timeline.
Consumer segment volumes declined; recovery depends on binder and synthetic grass prices.
Q2 FY27 monsoon-related seasonality in infrastructure; capacity ramp-ups of TPO, rCB and PCMB must deliver to hit INR670-700 crores.
Management's margin guidance (18-20%) is well below the Q1 print (22%); watch for Q2 and Q3 margin normalisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the strategy, but guarded on forward numbers: management declined to confirm either 18% or 22% margin, and deflected several EPR accounting questions to email follow-ups.
key_quotes: We are delighted to share that we have commenced FY27 on a very strong note, delivering our best ever quarterly profitability.
I will neither confirm that we will achieve 18% nor will I confirm we will achieve 22%.
Our focus -- our core investment will remain India for the foreseeable future.
Our hedge comes from the fact that we cater to consumer business, industrial business, infra business, steel now PCMB and also TPO and rCB.
